data.description:
## Description

**What**: Implement the schema-equivalent parity test as a CI job that runs for the duration of the epic, comparing post-migration output against the deterministic golden corpus captured in S1. Asserts both schema conformance AND zero-dropped-findings (every pre-migration `critical` / `important` / `fragile` finding preserved by id/title; additive findings allowed). Register the job in `.github/required-checks.txt` so a parity failure blocks merge.

**Why**: SC3 of the epic. Parity is the structural safeguard that the bash→Python cutover preserves the review-gate's effective output. A non-blocking parity job lets drift land silently; a blocking job catches it but must also be properly removed at epic close (S7) including the required-checks entry.

**Scope**:
- IN: Parity-test CI job that loads the S1 golden corpus, runs the new Python runner against the same fixture diffs, and asserts (a) JSON schema conformance and (b) every pre-migration critical/important/fragile finding preserved by id/title (zero dropped); registration in `.github/required-checks.txt` so failure blocks merge; documentation of the parity-test contract in the job description.
- OUT: Removing the parity test at epic close (S7); golden corpus capture (S1); duration measurements (S1 baseline + S5 post-migration).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, a parity-test CI job runs against every PR for the duration of the epic. The job loads the S1 golden corpus (deterministic LLM request/response cassettes + expected findings JSON), executes the new Python runner against the same fixture diffs, and asserts JSON schema conformance.
  ← Satisfies: "Schema-equivalent reviewer-findings.json parity across the fixture corpus"
- When this story is complete, the parity test asserts that every pre-migration `critical` / `important` / `fragile` finding from the golden corpus is preserved by id/title in the new runner's output. Additive findings are allowed but no critical / important / fragile finding may be dropped. A drop fails the job.
  ← Satisfies: "The parity test additionally asserts zero dropped findings relative to the pre-migration baseline"
- When this story is complete, the parity-test job is registered in `.github/required-checks.txt` and `validate-required-checks.sh` confirms alignment. A parity failure blocks merge for the duration of the epic.
  ← Satisfies: parity-test enforces the gate it's meant to protect (red-team finding)

## Considerations

- [Testing] Parity must check zero-dropped findings AND schema shape — a shape-only check would pass even if severity was downgraded or critical findings were dropped in favor of new grounded ones (red-team finding).
- [Reliability] Determinism of parity comparison depends on S1 capturing recorded provider responses (not just bash output). If S1's golden corpus is not deterministic, parity becomes a coin flip against live LLM drift.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As an engineer, a parity-test CI job blocks merges that drop critical findings vs. the pre-migration baseline
